analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: NVDA Beat, HFs De-risking Continues, Cyber Concerns Rising (18 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Nvidia rose 3% after hours on stronger results and guidance. FY2028 revenue growth guidance rose to about 75% from 70%, implying roughly $741bn of revenue and close to $17 of EPS. The Street is at $16 and buyside expectations are $18.

Nvidia says demand still exceeds supply, with better order visibility and secured memory and packaging capacity. Vera Rubin generated nearly $20bn in its first quarter, and CPU revenue is expected to more than double in FY2028, driven by agentic AI.
Nvidia expects gross margins to bottom at 71-72% in January as memory costs rise, then settle at 72-73% in FY2028.

Nvidia's financial commitments to customers and supply chain partners total $518bn, up from $366bn last quarter. Supply chain and capacity commitments are $390bn (from $279bn), datacenter leases $74bn (from $25bn), cloud service agreements $28bn (from $29bn), equity investments $20bn (from $25bn) and CapEx $6bn (from $8bn).

Nvidia is more selective on customer financing. Investments, commitments and guarantees will prioritize projects with land, power, buildings and clear demand, and guarantees take effect only once projects are ready. Goldman says this helps Nvidia's balance sheet but could make funding harder for leveraged neoclouds that rely on its backing, widening the gap with investment-grade hyperscalers.
Nvidia has about $227bn of buyback authorization remaining. Export restrictions remain a risk.
Global Fundamental L/S hedge funds are down 0.2% in November (+8.9% YTD as of Nov 16). Systematic L/S funds are up 1.1% month to date after a sharp recovery last week.

Hedge funds have heavily net sold global equities in November, with long and short sales at roughly 3 to 1. Selling in global Info Tech over the trailing 6 weeks since early October is the fastest in the past decade (-4.4 z-score), led by Semis & Semi Equipment. Industrials is the second most net sold US sector month to date.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell another 7.6 points month to date to its lowest level in more than five years, below the Liberation Day lows.

Exposure to medium-term momentum is on track to fall for a 6th straight month to its lowest since Dec 2022 (20th percentile over 5 years). Exposure to Value has risen sharply to 5-year highs amid increased stagflation concerns.

Recent outages include Microsoft 365 (Nov 12-14), with Microsoft reportedly saying it did not suspect malicious activity, plus FAA, JPMorgan Chase transaction and Apple service disruptions. An NSA classified internal network outage was reported Nov 17, attributed to routine maintenance or software upgrades.

Armbrust relays an investor theory that Eastern countries could be behind the outages as a pressure tactic ahead of Trump's meetings in Shenzhen, but is skeptical: the timing is peculiar and the evidence does not point to cyberattacks. His view is that cybersecurity services demand will keep rising quickly.
